name: Rusty-cheeked Hornbill
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar and southeastern thailand
description: Brownish, medium-sized hornbill. Male is dusty brown above and rusty-colored below, with a pale bill and blue-gray skin around the eye.

name: African Hawk-Eagle
rangeDescription: Woodland and savanna of sub-saharan africa
description: A medium-sized, boldly-patterned, dark-and-white eagle. In flight the underwing is brown and white with a thick black hind edge, and the tail is mostly pale gray with a thick dark bar at the end; these combine to give it a unique plumage pattern in flight.

name: Apurimac Spinetail
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (bosque de ampay region of apurímac)
description: Small, long-tailed bird found locally in humid montane forest in the Apurimac valley. Dark slaty gray with a rusty red cap and wings.

name: White-throated Swallow
rangeDescription: Angola to southeastern democratic republic of the congo, botswana, zambia, malawi, and south africa
description: A swallow with a small rufous patch on the forehead and a diagnostic complete steel-blue breast band which forms a white throat patch. This migrant breeds in South Africa in the Austral summer, September to April, and spends the non-breeding period (May to August) in south-central Africa.

name: Blue-capped Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Forest of mindanao (southern philippines)
description: A spectacular medium-sized kingfisher of foothill and montane forest on Mindanao with a thick red bill, a white throat, a blue rump, and faintly scaled rufous on the underparts and cheek, extending around the back of the neck. The male has a blue crown, blue tail, and blue wings with buff spots.

name: Cape Starling
rangeDescription: Acacia of western gabon and angola to south africa
description: A medium-sized iridescent blue-green glossy starling that lacks dark ear-patches and has greenish flanks and belly, giving it a more uniform appearance than the “blue-eared” starlings. Pairs and small groups occupy high-altitude grassland, Karoo, and savanna, including drier habitats than other glossy starlings.

name: White-throated Robin
rangeDescription: Türkiye, southern caucasus, and levant eastward to iran, and from southern kazakhstan and tajikistan to western and northern afghanistan; possibly also central uzbekistan; winters in northeastern and eastern africa
description: Large, long-billed robin that spends much of its time on the ground with tail cocked. The male has bluish upperparts, a dark face, a white supercilium, a broad black tail, and bright orange underparts.

name: Gorgeous Sunbird
rangeDescription: Western, central, and southern kenya and tanzania
description: A slim, long-billed sunbird in which breeding males and females are very different. Breeding males are mostly dark green with a red-and-yellow band across the underparts, and a black belly.

name: Junin Canastero
rangeDescription: Very local in andes of central and southern peru
description: Chunky, streaked brown bird with a long tail that is often held cocked. Warm reddish brown with extensive white streaking through its head, back, and sides.

name: Biak Hooded Pitta
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Beautiful leaf-green pitta of Biak Island, off northwestern New Guinea. Like the other “Hooded-type” pittas with which it was formerly grouped, this species has a black head, powder-blue shoulder patch, and red on the lower belly and undertail.

name: Red-crowned Amazon
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern mexico (nuevo león to northern veracruz)
description: Fairly large, bright green parrot endemic to humid tropical lowlands and foothills in northeast Mexico. Uncommon.

name: Tocuyo Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of northeastern colombia and northwestern venezuela
description: A large sparrow with bold black stripes on a gray head, olive-brown upperparts, and whitish underparts with buffy gray tinge. Eyebrow whitish, usually paler face and median crown stripe.

name: Sao Tome Paradise-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: São tomé island (gulf of guinea)
description: A distinctive long-tailed paradise-flycatcher with different-looking sexes. Male is glossy blue-black with a pale blue bill and blue eye-rings; female has a dark crown, a gray face, rusty upperparts, and pale underparts.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Grande Comore Brush-Warbler
rangeDescription: Forest undergrowth of grand comoro island
description: A robust, medium-sized brown bird with a long, spiky tail. Endemic to the island of Grand Comoro.

name: Whooping Crane
rangeDescription: Breeds northern canada; winters coastal southeastern texas
description: Larger, pure white, rare cousin of the Sandhill Crane. One of the tallest birds in North America, striking and unmistakable: brilliant white overall with black wingtips and a red crown and mustache.

name: Eastern Bearded-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Cameroon to eastern democratic republic of the congo, northern angola, and far western uganda
description: A large greenbul often found in family groups or flocks in forest and forest edge with other bearded-greenbuls. Like all bearded-greenbuls, will sometimes puff out throat feathers.

name: Bolivian Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia and adjacent northwestern argentina (jujuy)
description: Striking tanager of open woodland and scrub in high elevations of the east slope of the Andes in central and southern Bolivia and extreme NW Argentina; including agricultural lands, and open Polylepis woodland. From Black-and-chestnut Warbling-Finch by white throat and paler underparts in Bolivian.

name: Caroline Islands Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Montane forest of eastern caroline islands (chuuk and pohnpei)
description: Beautiful dark velvet dove with a pristine white face, throat, and breast. Endemic to Chuuk and Pohnpei, in the Caroline Islands group.

name: Yellow-collared Lovebird
rangeDescription: Tanzania
description: A colorful lovebird of East African savanna that is also found in woodland, cultivated areas, and around human habitation. Note the green back, the broad yellow collar, the black face, and the red bill.

name: Gray-cheeked Tit-Babbler
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern java
description: Small drab Javan endemic. Generally local and uncommon in declining lowland forest and forest edge habitats.
